The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Shashikala W/o Rajagopala in the road traffic accident that took place on 23.11.2024.
2.

The brief facts of the petition are as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that, on 23.11.2024 at about 07.45 p.m., the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider in motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-J-9148 proceeding on Sulibele Lake at Sulibele village and Hobli, Hosakote Taluk,
Bangalore.

The deceased husband was riding slowly carefully, cautiously, observing the traffic rules, at that time a Tanker Lorry Car bearing Reg. No. TN-52-K-3460 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came at a high speed and dashed to the deceased motorcycle.
As a result of the forced impact, deceased and rider were fell-down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, the injured was taken to Manipal Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient, but inspite of better treatment deceased was died in the Hospital on same day.

Thereafter the body was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Hosakote for postmortem and the body was handed over to the petitioners, the petitioners shifted the dead body to their native place and also performed the last rites and obsequies ceremony and they have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/-
towards medical and funeral expenses.

On account of the sudden and sad demise of the deceased in Rajagopala vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89781977/
2 the said accident, the petitioners have undergoing deep mental shock and mental agony and hardship.

sentences.text: Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 57 years and she was working as Coolie and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband of the deceased and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased, so the petitioners have lost their family member.
The petitioners were solely depending upon the income of the deceased.
The respondents are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay Rs.50,00,000/- with cost and interest to the petitioners.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.

The respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed his written statement and denied the case of the petitioners as false and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.
This respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy and policy is in-force.
It is further submitted that, at the time of accident the driver of Lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-52-3460 possessed effective valid driving license to drive the vehicle.

It is further submitted that, at the time of accident the lorry in question involved in the accident was not possessed FC and permit as such insurer is not liable to pay indemnify the insured under policy.

Further, this respondent denied the age,
occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 23.11.2024 at about 7.45 p.m., accident took place near Sulibele Lake at Sulibele village and Hobli, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru,
due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Tanker Lorry Car bearing Reg. No.
TN-52-K-3460 as a result deceased has succumbed to the accidental injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
5. In order order to prove the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.

6. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the material placed on record.
7.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
 Issue No.1 ...

In the affirmative,

:REASONS:
 8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioners contended that on 23.11.2024 at about 07.45 p.m. deceased Shashikala W/o Rajagopala met with road traffic accident and died due to rash and negligent driving for driver of Tanker Lorry Car bearing Reg. No.
TN-52-K-3460.

The burden is upon the petitioners to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the Tanker Lorry Car bearing Reg. No. TN-52-K-3460 .
9.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband of the deceased, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased Shashikala.

The claimants/petitioners, in order to prove that, the occurrence of road traffic accident as contended by them in their claim petition has occurred on the date, time and place and in the manner as contended by them in their claim petition, got examined petitioner No.1 - the husband of the deceased as PW.1 and reiterated the petition averments and got marked the documents at Exs.P.1 to 15.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Sketch, Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.5 is the Inquest Report, Ex.P.6 is the Postmortem Report, Ex.P.7 is the charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 is the IP Bill, Ex.P.9 to Ex.P.11 are the Notarized copies of Aadhar Card of petitioners, Ex.P.12 is the Vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P.13 is the Notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.14 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.15 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of deceased.
10. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Sulibele Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 145/2024.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.
11.
Ex.P.1 to 7 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the Tanker Lorry driver.

The Ex.P.3 (sketch) clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.7, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the Tanker Lorry U/s. 279 and 304-A of IPC.
The Ex.P.4 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

Moreover,
learned counsel for insurance company has taken defence that, the alleged accident is not caused due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending vehicle.

On going through the materials available on record it reveals that, except suggestions during the cross examination of PW.1,
insurance company has not produced any material before this court in support of their contention.
12. In this case, none of the contesting parties failed to prove that, accident is not caused due to the driver of offending vehicle.

Hence, having regard to the above facts and circumstances, this court opine that, accident is caused solely due to negligence of driver of Tanker Lorry Car bearing Reg. No.
Rajagopala vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89781977/
4 TN-52-K-3460 .
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.2: This Issue is regarding dependency, quantum of compensation to be awarded to petitioners and who is liable to pay the same, which is answered under the following heads:
14 . LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
To ascertain the actual loss of dependency, the age, income of deceased and the number of dependents of the deceased are to be taken into consideration.

It is the contention of the petitioners that they are solely depending upon the income of the deceased and due to death of Shashikala W/o Rajagopala, they have lost love and affection of the deceased.
15. The petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased Shashikala.
The deceased out of her income contributed to the income of family consisting of herself and petitioners herein.

On going through the materials available on record, either of the parties failed to produce the oral or documentary evidence to show that, petitioner No.2 and 3 are not dependent on the income of deceased Shashikala.
Hence, this Tribunal opine that, all the petitioners are the dependents on the income of deceased and hence 1/3 of the income should be taken towards personal expenses of the deceased.

16. Considering recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Special leave petitioner (Civil No.25590/2014 dated:31.10.2016(National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others), in which it is observed that, "in case if the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation".

17. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., & Others),
Wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, there can not be distinction where there is evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guesswork, as such addition on account of future prospects is admissible where in the absence of proof of income.

sentences.text: 18. The petitioners contended that, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged 57 years and was working as Coolie and she was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The petitioners have produced the postmortem report of deceased Shashikala which is marked at Ex.P.6.
From perusal of the Ex.P.6 age of the deceased is mentioned as 57 Years as on the date of accident.
Hence, the age of the deceased is considered as 57 years as on the date of accident.
The accident took place in the year 2024.
In this case in order to prove income of the deceased petitioners have not produced any documents before this court.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,500/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2024 at Rs.16,500/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka,
Bengaluru Bench.
The accident is of the year is 2024.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- p.m. as per above decision.

sentences.text: As per decision stated above, it is clear that, the Tribunal has to consider the future prospects on actual salary less tax and even for self employed or were engaged on fixed wages.
Admittedly, the age of the deceased is 57 years.
So 10% of future prospects is taken into consideration.

Taking into consideration of the same, if 10% is added to the income of the deceased it would be Rs.16,500/- +
10% of Rs.16,500/- is Rs.1,650/- = Rs.18,150/- per month.
There is only one dependent.
Hence, 1/3 has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
So, 1/3 of Rs.18,150/- would be Rs.6,050/-.
Income for consideration (Rs.18,150 - 6,050) is Rs.12,100/- per month.
Therefore the annual income (Rs.12,100 x 12) is Rs.1,45,200/-.
As such correct multiplier as per guidelines of Sarala Varma case would be "09".

Thus the loss of dependency works out to (Rs.1,45,200/- x 9) is Rs.13,06,800/-.
20.
TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY, FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:
The petitioners have spent the amount towards shifting the dead body and performing funeral and obsequies ceremony.

In this regard, the Hon'ble Supreme Court judgment passed in Special Leave petitioner (Civil) No.25590/2014 dated:31-10-2017 (National Insurance Co., Ltd Vs.
Pranaya Sethi and Others), wherein it is held that as far as conventional heads are concerned, the petitioners are entitled for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- and under the head of loss of estate at Rs.15,000/-.

sentences.text: 21. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

The petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased, so they are entitled for consortium for loss of "protection, affection,
society, discipline, guidance and training".
Therefore, Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to the petitioners under the head of loss of consortium.

22. ESCALATION OF 10% ON AMOUNT AWARDED UNDER CONVENTIONAL HEADS:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court at para No.59.8 of Judgment passed in Pranaya Sethi and others has directed to enhance the amount to be awarded under conventional heads to an extent of 10% on every 03 years.

Further more, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a decision delivered on 07.07.2021 in MFA No.101723/2017 clubbed with MFA No.104014/2016 between Smt. Viday @ Vidyashree W/o Bandu @ Dattu Koli and others Vs. Sanju S/o Veerappa Koli and another at paragraph No.16 has awarded 10% of enhanced amount on total amount awarded under conventional heads.
The Judgment in Pranya Sethi (referred supra) delivered on 31.10.2017, as such 06 years have lapsed.
Thus the petitioners are entitled for 20% enhanced amount under the above conventional heads.
While discussing above, this tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- under conventional heads and 20% of the same comes to Rs.24,000/-.
Thus, petitioners are entitled for an amount of Rs.24,000/- under this head.

Considering the above facts and for the above reasons, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1 Loss of dependency Rs.13,06,800/-

24,000/-
conventional heads Total Rs.14,80,800/-
Hence, this Tribunal feels to award just and proper compensation of Rs.14,80,800/- to the petitioners.
23. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg. No. TN-52-K-3460 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 30.10.2024 to 29.10.2025.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 23.11.2024.

Hence,
policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
24. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied In a decision in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

sentences.text: Accordingly, ISSUE No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion and findings, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are awarded with compensation of Rs.14,80,800/- with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
After deposit of compensation amount, share of compensation is apportioned in the ratio of 60:20:20.

Out of compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.1 70% of the amount shall be released infavour of the petitioner No.1 and remaining 30% of the amount shall be deposited as FD in the name of petitioner No.1 in any Nationalised or Schedule Bank for a period of 03 years on proper identification.
